Garrett Lisi defined a "universal reservoir" for a quantum mechanical analogue of this quantity, which can be produced by Wick rotations on a Feynman path integral. One principle describing this quantity can be unified with the maximum entropy principle since path uncertainty can be measured by the Shannon information. General relativity uses the Einstein-Hilbert type of this quantity which yields the Einstein field equations, and the shape of the trajectory of this quantity over two specific endpoints is determined through Maupertuis' principle. The Euler-Lagrange equation for this quantity of a system yields the evolution of a classical system, and the functional derivative of this quantity with respect to generalized coordinates goes to zero in accordance with Hamilton's principle. For 10 points, identify this quantity which is defined as the time integral over a given path of the Lagrangian of a system, and is symbolizes S.

During the Revolutionary War, this state was the site of a failed attempt by John Sullivan to recapture Aquidneck Island. This state was the site of the Great Swamp Fight, and later saw the death of the Wampanoag leader Metacomet in King Philip's War. It also saw an incident where the Sons of Liberty raided and burned the grounded HMS Gaspée. Samuel Ward King opposed electoral reform in this state, leading to the Dorr Rebellion, and it was home to the Narragansetts. For 10 points, name this state founded by an exile from Massachusetts, Roger Williams, who named it after a Greek island.

William Widgery Thomas encouraged Protestant Swedes to settle in the north of this state. After an 1854 anti-Catholic riot in this state's town of Bath, the Know-Nothing party became prominent here due to its large numbers of French and Irish Catholics. A politician who represented this state names a proposed amendment to public funding for parochial schools. This state's holding of elections for Governor, Senators, and congressmen in September gave rise to the saying "As [this state] goes, so goes the nation" though some say it was because in 1851, Protestants in this state got it to become the first to ban alcohol. A politician from this state had his presidential hopes crushed when a supporter called the Democrats the party of "Rum, Romanism, and Rebellion" in 1884. For 10 points, identify this state represented by "Plumed Knight" James G. Blaine.

Located twelve miles from the Pacific Ocean, this lake also contains a population of bull sharks, which were once thought to be its own species. It drains into the Caribbean Sea via the San Juan River, which Cornelius Vanderbilt used along with this lake to create an ocean-to-ocean route before the Panama Canal was built. For 10 points, identify this lake, the largest in Central America, which is named after a country with its capital at Managua.
